input.task: Which product on this page costs $24.50?

provenance:
the offline twin of live-hn-item1-submitter: the same contract-advertised `near:` key (specs/001 §TraceStep target schema), on a fixture, so the mechanism is graded in the fast suite where live cases never gate. Ground truth is literal in src/browser/fixtures/shop.html: the row `
  • Meridian Wall Clock $24.50
    • `. The anchor text PRECEDES nothing — the link comes before the price — so this grades the backward direction of proximity, where HN's subline ('N points by pg') grades the forward one. 'the product name next to this price' is a browsing primitive, not site knowledge (CLAUDE.md rule 6): no selector, no DOM path, only a role and a visible string.

triage.watched_red: red until the resolver implements `near:`. Today the key is dropped silently, leaving a bare {role: link} against four catalogue links -> ResolveError ambiguous-match -> failure:locate. That silent drop is itself a defect with its own case (resolver-unknown-target-key).
triage.anchor_corrected: the identity anchor was first written as 'Meridian Wall Clock' — the case's own expected answer, which the `grounded` check already asserts is in the evidence. That made `identity_anchors` a check that could not go red, the exact shape verifier-anchor-not-self-satisfied exists to forbid, reintroduced at the case level instead of the code level (M6 cold review). It anchors on the price now: the entity the task names, independent of the answer.
triage.narrow_margin: this case passes on a one-element margin (the product link is one element before the price, the next product's link two after). A row with anything after the price — a CTA, a rating, a badge — makes those distances equal, which is a different question with its own case: near-equidistant-is-ambiguous.
